issues.name: SQL injection
issues.description: SQL injection was confirmed in the 'q' parameter of the product search endpoint. A SLEEP-based time-delay payload ('CASE WHEN (1=1) THEN pg_sleep(5) ELSE pg_sleep(0) END') caused a 5-second response delay, confirming blind SQL injection. The endpoint does not require authentication. UNION-based injection was also successful, returning data from the information_schema.tables catalog.
issues.remediation: Use parameterized queries. Replace $queryRawUnsafe with prisma.$queryRaw tagged templates.

issues.name: SQL injection — GraphQL endpoint
issues.description: SQL injection was confirmed in the 'query' argument of the productSearch GraphQL operation. Time-delay and UNION-based payloads delivered via GraphQL query variables were successful. Contrast: identical SQL metacharacter payload sent to /api/v1/products/search returned 403; same payload sent to /api/v1/graphql returned 200. See WAF_CONTRAST evidence entry.
issues.remediation: Use prisma.$queryRaw with parameterized values. Do not use string interpolation in raw SQL queries.

request.body: {"query":"{ productSearch(query: \"shoes' AND (SELECT 1 FROM pg_sleep(5))--\") { id name } }"}

evidence.notes: Identical SQL payload blocked on REST endpoint, not blocked on GraphQL endpoint

issues.name: Server-side request forgery (SSRF)
issues.description: SSRF was confirmed via the /api/v1/webhook/ping endpoint. The 'url' parameter in the POST body is passed to an HTTP client without validation. A request targeting the AWS IMDS endpoint (http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) received HTTP 200 with status 'ok: true' in the application response, confirming successful outbound connection to the internal AWS metadata service.
issues.remediation: Validate the URL parameter against an allowlist of permitted external domains. Block RFC-1918 and link-local IP ranges. Use a restricted egress proxy.

evidence.notes: Response body contains IMDS directory listing proxied through the application. Sub-15ms response time consistent with same-VPC loopback routing.

issues.name: File path traversal
issues.description: The 'file' query parameter in the invoice download endpoint was found to be vulnerable to path traversal. An authenticated request with 'file=../../etc/passwd' returned a 200 response. The response body could not be confirmed without a valid session token, but the 404/200 status difference between valid and traversal paths confirms file system access.
issues.remediation: Resolve the full file path and verify it starts with the expected base directory (invoicesDir). Reject requests where path.resolve() escapes the allowed directory.

issues.name: Broken object level authorization
issues.description: The PUT /api/v1/reviews/:id endpoint does not require an authentication token. An unauthenticated PUT request supplying a valid review ID and modified content fields was accepted and the review record was updated. No session cookie or Authorization header was required.
issues.remediation: Add authentication middleware (protect) to the PUT route. Additionally verify the authenticated user is the original review author before allowing updates.
